figures.finding: Directors in Mumbai's film and television industry join the Indian Film & Television Directors' Association (IFTDA), which calls its membership mandatory; a director pays Rs 25,001 to join (an assistant director Rs 2,951), must show credits or a producer's letter, and must carry the card for inspection by IFTDA or the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE).

value.proof: credit titles (booklet/IMDb) or a producer's or channel's letter for work in production
value.renewal: card has a validity date; penalty after 2 years unpaid

figures.applies: India, Hindi-language film and television centred on Mumbai; read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Indian Film & Television Directors’ Association, having its office in Mumbai enrols Directors, Assistant Directors, Creative Directors, Assistant Creative Directors, Associate Creative Directors, Casting Directors and Assistant Casting Directors who thereafter have the liberty to work in the entertainment industry without any restriction from any other film body. … THE MEMBERSHIP OF IFTDA IS MANDATORY.

I) Booklet/IMDB page/ link containing his/her credit titles in case of feature film. II) In case of an under production work, a letter from the Producer / Channel stating the name of Feature film/ documentary film/short film/advertisement film/ TV Serial for which the applicant has been employed or working. … c) The membership card should be available with the members while on duty and should be produced on demand by the authorized representative of IFTDA or Federation of Western India Cine Employees. … e) Membership Fees for new member has been fixed at Rs. 25,001/- (Rs. Twenty Five Thousand One Only) … RIGHT TO VOTE ONLY FOR REGULAR MEMBERS AFTER ONE YEAR OF ENROLMENT THREE YEARS ENROLMENT MANDATORY FOR SEEKING ELECTION TO THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE
e) Membership Fees for new member has been fixed at Rs. 2,951/- (Rs. Two Thousand Nine Hundred Fifty One Only)

figures.finding: IFTDA states no fee agreement; what it offers on pay is a Dispute Settlement Committee that meets regularly to settle members' disputes with producers and recover unpaid remuneration.

value.arbitration: members undertake to abide by IFTDA arbitration in any dispute

sources.said: The Dispute Settlement Committee meetings are regularly convened to solve the dispute matters of our members with Producers and help them recover their hard earned remuneration dues.
In case of any dispute matter, I undertake to abide by decision of the Arbitration of IFTDA

figures.finding: Indian copyright law makes the producer, not the director, the author of a cinematograph film, the producer being whoever takes the initiative and responsibility for making it; so the film's final form is the producer's.

value.textRead: consolidation to Act No. 49 of 1999 (WIPO Lex IN007)

figures.applies: India; text as consolidated to the 1999 amendment. WIPO Lex lists a consolidation to Act No. 18 of 2023, but its PDF was served as an HTML page and indiacode.nic.in did not answer, so later amendments were not read.

sources.said: "author" means,- (i) in relation to a literary or dramatic work, the author of the work; (ii) in relation to a musical work, the composer; (iii) in relation to an artistic work other than a photograph, the artist; (iv) relation to a photograph, the person taking the photograph; (v) in relation to a cinematograph film or sound recording, the producer; … "producer", in relation to a cinematograph film or sound recording, means a person who takes the initiative and responsibility for making the work;
